front: What property must every node satisfy in a binary max-heap?
back: Every parent's value is ≥ both its children's values.

front: Where is the maximum element always located in a binary max-heap?
Is a binary max-heap a binary search tree?
back: No — a heap only enforces parent ≥ child locally; it has no left-vs-right ordering, so it is never a valid BST once it has more than 2 nodes.

front: What is the complexity of building a heap from an unsorted array?
back: Θ(n) — not O(n log n) — via a bottom-up sift-down (heapify) from the last non-leaf node to the root.

front: Why does BuildHeap only call heapify on the first half of the array?
back: By definition of a complete tree, roughly the last ⌈n/2⌉ indices are leaves — they have no children, so heapify on them is a guaranteed no-op.

front: Why must BuildHeap process indices bottom-up (highest to lowest), not top-down?
back: heapify(A, i) is only correct if both children of i are already valid heaps. Top-down would fix the root first — before its subtrees are heaps — so larger values buried two levels down could never bubble past the top, producing an invalid heap.

front: Heap Insert(H, k) — what are the two steps?
back: 1) Append k at the last free array slot (keeps the tree complete). 2) Sift-up: swap k with its parent while the parent is smaller, until the heap property holds or the root is reached.

front: Why is append(H,k) + full BuildHeap(H.A) a valid but wasteful way to implement Insert?
back: It re-checks ~n/2 nodes (Θ(n)) to fix what a single sift-up path already handles in O(log n) — correct, just asymptotically worse per insertion.

front: Heap extract-max — what are the three steps?
back: 1) Save the root as the max. 2) Move the last element into the root, shrink the array by one. 3) Sift-down (heapify) from the root to restore the heap property.

front: During sift-down, when the current node is smaller than a child, which child do you swap with?
back: The larger of the two children — swapping with the smaller child would not fix the heap property on that side.

front: Is Heap Sort stable? Is it in-place?
back: Not stable (swaps can reorder equal keys). In-place (O(1) extra space) — Θ(n log n).

front: For a 0-indexed array heap, what are the parent/left-child/right-child index formulas for node i?
Do heap insert or extract-max ever perform a rotation?
back: No — only element swaps along a single root-to-leaf or leaf-to-root path. Rotation is an AVL/RBT/Splay-tree concept, not a heap one.
